what_its_for: Acetohydroxamic acid is used to help prevent certain types of kidney stones from growing. It works by blocking a substance in your urine that allows bacteria to make your urine less acidic, which is what causes these special stones (called struvite or infection stones) to form. It is usually used along with antibiotics and sometimes other treatments.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth, on an empty stomach, 1 hour before or 2 hours after meals. Swallow the tablets whole with a full glass of water. Try to take your doses at the same times each day to keep a steady amount of the medicine in your body. Do not crush or chew the tablets.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 250 mg taken 3 to 4 times a day, for a total of 750 mg to 1,500 mg per day. Your doctor will decide the exact dose that is right for you based on your kidney function and how well you respond to treatment. Never change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store this medicine at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine past the expiration date printed on the label.
what_to_avoid: Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine. Drinking alcohol can cause a serious reaction including flushing, fast heartbeat, nausea, and low blood pressure. Avoid becoming pregnant while taking this medicine, as it can harm an unborn baby. Use reliable birth control during treatment and talk to your doctor about your options. Avoid iron supplements or products containing iron unless your doctor tells you it is okay, since iron can block this medicine from working properly.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you notice any of the following: unusual bruising or bleeding, blood clots in your legs (pain, swelling, or redness in your leg), chest pain or shortness of breath, severe headache, numbness or tingling in your hands or feet, skin rash, hair loss, or yellowing of your skin or eyes. Also call your doctor if you feel very tired, dizzy, or if you think you might be pregnant.
when_it_works: This medicine works slowly over time. It does not dissolve kidney stones that are already there, but it helps stop them from getting bigger and may help prevent new ones from forming. You may not feel any different right away, but your doctor will monitor your progress with urine and blood tests. It may take several weeks to months to see the full benefit.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Do NOT take this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. It can cause serious birth defects and harm to the baby. Women who can become pregnant must use reliable birth control during treatment. Breastfeeding: It is not known if this medicine passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Kidney problems: If your kidneys do not work well, your doctor will give you a lower dose or may tell you not to use this medicine at all. Children: This medicine is sometimes used in children, but the dose will be carefully adjusted by your doctor based on body weight. Elderly patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects and should be monitored closely by their doctor.
